Adding a quantity/stance channel to the Cartographer relation detector raised its contradiction precision on a synthetic same-story corpus without losing recall.

MEASURED LINKED #priceriot-calibration-holdout as of 2026-11-25

In a leakage-free 21-day to 7-day held-out calibration over synthetic Cowboy Market POS data (N=5 seeds), transferring only the fitted spawn interval (449.13s) matched 6 schedule-aligned Mon-Sat open days within -3.22% transactions and +4.03% revenue with 0.0325 intraday period TVD, while exposing uncalibrated SKU-mix limits (38% top-10 overlap) and a Sunday schedule mismatch (-15.23% across all 7 calendar days).

Does not showFit to real (non-synthetic) store foot traffic or POS receipts: cowboy_pos.csv is synthetically generated. The SKU-mix and basket-size gaps reflect that extract_params() only transfers spawn_interval_seconds into the C++ engine.

MEASURED LINKED #priceriot-pricing-elasticity as of 2026-11-25

In a controlled dynamic-pricing experiment via set_sku_price across 5 seeds (target SKUs 1-5 vs control SKUs 6-30), target demand declined monotonically from 130.0 units at 0.75x to 9.4 units at 3.00x (implied arc elasticity -0.414 to -0.941) while control-group volume stayed stable (364.2-390.8 units).

Does not showReal-world shopper price sensitivity: this verifies the C++17 behavioral acceptance curve and control-SKU isolation under synthetic simulation parameters.

BUILT LINKED #priceriot-engine as of 2026-11-25

PriceRiot is a headless-capable C++17 retail-store simulation exposed to Python via pybind11: customer and worker agents pathfind (A* on a navmesh) through a YAML-defined store, respond to per-SKU dynamic pricing, and emit synthetic transaction records.

Does not showCalibration to a real (non-synthetic) store's foot traffic or sales; the held-out calibration run in priceriot-calibration-holdout uses synthetic POS data.
